# 🚇 **Chronological Timeline of Line B – Buenos Aires Underground**  
*Color-Coded Phases for Memory & Recall*

## 🟦 **Phase 1: Foundation & Legal Origins (1912–1927)**  
*Establishing the legal and financial groundwork for the line*

| Date | Event | Key Details |
|------|-------|-------------|
| **1912** | 📜 **Law 8,870 Enacted** | Congress of Argentina passes the law to build a subway connecting Correo Central to Triunvirato & Elcano, linking with the Ferrocarril Central de Buenos Aires (FCCBA). Goal: reduce central city traffic. |
| **1927** | 💼 **Financial Agreement Signed in NYC** | Teófilo Lacroze, Banco de la Nación, and bankers Harris & Forbes sign a deal granting Lacroze Brothers Company a 50-year concession for passengers, parcels, and freight. |
| **1927–1930** | 🏗️ **Construction Begins** | Built by Dwight P. Robinson & Cía. Line named *Ferrocarril Terminal Central de Buenos Aires (FTCBA)*. |

> 🔍 **Memory Tip**: Think of "1912 – the law was signed like a contract; 1927 – the money was raised in New York; 1930 – construction finished."  
> 🎨 **Color**: Blue (Foundation)

---

## 🟨 **Phase 2: Opening & Early Operations (1930–1933)**  
*Launch of service, infrastructure, and early innovations*

| Date | Event | Key Details |
|------|-------|-------------|
| **17 October 1930** | 🚆 **First Section Opens** | First segment (Federico Lacroze to Callao) opens. 7.021 km long. Argentine President José Félix Uriburu takes the maiden ride. |
| **22 June 1931** | 🚆 **Extension to Carlos Pellegrini** | Line extended to Carlos Pellegrini station. |
| **1 December 1931** | 🏁 **Line Fully Completed** | Reaches Leandro N. Alem station. Total length: ~8.7 km. Built below Corrientes Avenue with 19 curves and 13 stations. |
| **1933** | 🚚 **Underground Link to Mercado Central de Abasto** | Electric freight wagons connect to the wholesale market. Service ends after a fire on **27 November 1952**. |
| **1930s** | 🚪 **First Turnstiles & Escalators** | Line B becomes the first to have turnstiles and moving stairways (coin-operated). Also features automatic light signaling. |

> 🔍 **Memory Tip**: "1930 – first ride; 1931 – grew; 1933 – linked to market; 1930s – first modern features."  
> 🎨 **Color**: Yellow (Launch & Innovation)
